assumptions.condition: \(Q[\rho(x)\{S_{\mathrm{pot}}(1)-S_{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\}\ge0\mid C,X=x]=1\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) with \(Q(C\mid X=x)>0\).

assumptions.condition: \(\epsilon\le Q(Z=1\mid X=x)\le1-\epsilon\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) with \(Q(X=x)>0\).

standard.name: fixed-\(\epsilon\) uniform-class strengthening of Dong--Heiler instrument-propensity overlap
uniform-class strengthening of the inherited positive survivor-complier denominator condition

definitions.name: Total algebraic survivor-capacity map
definitions.construction: For \(u,v\in\mathbb R\), set \(u\oslash v=u/v\) if \(v\ne0\) and \(u\oslash0=0\). For every \(q\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\), set \(q_{xz}(q)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}q_{xza}\) and \(q_x(q)=\sum_{z,a}q_{xza}\). For \(k\in\mathcal Y\), define \(R_{0kx}(q)=q_{x0,(0,1,k)}\oslash q_{x0}(q)-q_{x1,(0,1,k)}\oslash q_{x1}(q)\) and \(R_{1kx}(q)=q_{x1,(1,1,k)}\oslash q_{x1}(q)-q_{x0,(1,1,k)}\oslash q_{x0}(q)\), and set \(H_x(q)=q_x(q)\{R_{0\cdot x}(q)_+,R_{1\cdot x}(q)_+\}\in\mathbb R^{2K}\). For every \((\ell,h)\in\mathbb R^{2K}\), let \(s_0=\sum_k\ell_k\), \(s_1=\sum_k h_k\), \(m(\ell,h)=\min(s_0,s_1)\), \(F_L(\ell,h)=\max\{0,\max_{0\le t<K}(\sum_{k\le t}\ell_k-\sum_{k\le t}h_k)+\min(s_1-s_0,0)\}\), and \(F_U(\ell,h)=\min\{m(\ell,h),\min_{0\le t<K}(\sum_{k<t}\ell_k+\sum_{k>t}h_k)\}\). Define \(\bar M(q)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}m\{H_x(q)\}\), \(\bar N_L(q)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}F_L\{H_x(q)\}\), and \(\bar N_U(q)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}F_U\{H_x(q)\}\), and use \(M(q)=\bar M(q)\).

definitions.name: Legal full-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{Q:Q\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:conditional-iv-independence},\text{ass:consistency},\text{ass:selection-consistency},\text{ass:outcome-consistency},\text{ass:no-defiers},\text{ass:cellwise-selection-monotonicity},\text{ass:instrument-overlap},\text{ass:aggregate-survivor-mass}\}\). Treatment indexing of \(S_{\mathrm{pot}}\) and \(Y_{\mathrm{pot}}\), rather than an additional instrument index plus exclusion assumptions, is the structural convention inherited from the accepted identification substrate.

definitions.name: Imported sharp endpoint map and total extension
definitions.construction: For every \(q\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\), define \(\bar\Phi(q)=\{\bar N_L(q)/\bar M(q),\bar N_U(q)/\bar M(q)\}\) when \(\bar M(q)>0\), and \(\bar\Phi(q)=(0,1)\) otherwise; set \(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}=\bar\Phi\). The accepted \(\text{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport}\) sharp exact-mass threshold theorem, cited as AcceptedSlateBenefit2026, supplies the identification substrate: for every \(q=p_Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(M(q)=\bar M(q)\ge m_*\), \(\Phi(q)=\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(q)=(L(q),U(q))\), \(L(q)=\bar N_L(q)/\bar M(q)\), and \(U(q)=\bar N_U(q)/\bar M(q)\).

definitions.name: Total nearby-legal-base directional envelope
definitions.construction: For each \(b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), set \(\mathcal D_b=\{g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}:q_{xz}(b)=0\text{ and }q_{xz}(g)=0\Longrightarrow g_{xza}=0\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A,\ x\in\mathcal X,\ z\in\{0,1\}\}\). Define \(d_b(g)=\partial_+\bar\Phi(b;g)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\{\bar\Phi(b+tg)-\bar\Phi(b)\}/t\) for every \(g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\). Set \(B_n=\{b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}:\|b-\widehat p_n\|_\infty\le a_n\}\). Define \(T_n(g)=\sup_{b\in B_n}\|d_b(g)\|_\infty\) when \(B_n\ne\varnothing\), and \(T_n(g)=0\) when \(B_n=\varnothing\). Values \(d_b(g)\) for \(g\notin\mathcal D_b\) are total calibration scaffolding only.

definitions.name: Total common-Gaussian max-norm rectangle
definitions.construction: Let \(W^*\sim N(0,I_{|\mathcal J|})\) be independent of the data and set \(G^*=\Sigma(\widehat p_n)^{1/2}W^*\), using the principal positive-semidefinite square root. With the lower-quantile convention, set \(c_n=\inf\{t\in[0,\infty):\Pr\{T_n(G^*)\le t\mid\widehat p_n\}\ge1-\alpha\}\). If \(B_n=\varnothing\) or \(M(\widehat p_n)=0\), set \(C_n=\mathbb R^2\). Otherwise set \(C_n=\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(\widehat p_n)+[-c_n,c_n]^2/\sqrt n\). This full-plane branch is an honest finite-sample fallback, including \(M(\widehat p_n)=0\) with \(B_n\ne\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Deterministic inner-neighborhood envelope
definitions.construction: For \(p\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(r>0\), set \(\mathcal B(p,r)=\{b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}:\|b-p\|_\infty\le r\}\) and \(E_{p,r}(g)=\sup_{b\in\mathcal B(p,r)}\|d_b(g)\|_\infty\).

definitions.name: Separated regular face
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Reg}(p)\) holds when the operative positive-part signs, survivor-total comparison, and nonredundant lower and upper threshold optimizers of \(\Phi\) are unique with strictly positive slack in a neighborhood of \(p\), and the ordinary derivative \(A_p\) exists with \(A_p\Sigma(p)A_p^{\mathsf T}\) positive definite.

definitions.name: Complete legal \(K=4\) kill-test array
definitions.construction: Fix sufficiently large \(n\), put \(r_n=n^{-1/2}\), \(\delta_n=2\lambda_{\mathrm r}/\{n(1-r_n)\}\), \(Q_n^{(4)}(X=0)=1-r_n\), \(Q_n^{(4)}(X=1)=r_n\), and draw \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) conditionally independently of all potential variables. Every unit has \(D_{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=0\) and \(D_{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\). Conditional on \(X=0\), give survivor response types \((S_{\mathrm{pot}}(0),S_{\mathrm{pot}}(1),Y_{\mathrm{pot}}(0),Y_{\mathrm{pot}}(1))=(1,1,k,k)\) masses \(\ell^0=(\delta_n,.10,.10-\delta_n,.05)\); give selection-gain types \((S_{\mathrm{pot}}(0),S_{\mathrm{pot}}(1),Y_{\mathrm{pot}}(0),Y_{\mathrm{pot}}(1))=(0,1,0,k)\) masses \(h^0-\ell^0=(.10-\delta_n,0,\delta_n,.15)\), where \(h^0=(.10,.10,.10,.20)\); and give the never-selected type \((0,0,0,0)\) mass \(.50\). Conditional on \(X=1\), use survivor masses \(\gamma_{ij}=2\ell_i^1h_j^1\) with \(\ell^1=(.05,.15,.20,.10)\), \(h^1=(.10,.15,.15,.10)\), namely \(\gamma=\begin{pmatrix}.010&.015&.015&.010\\.030&.045&.045&.030\\.040&.060&.060&.040\\.020&.030&.030&.020\end{pmatrix}\), and put the remaining mass \(.50\) on \((S_{\mathrm{pot}}(0),S_{\mathrm{pot}}(1),Y_{\mathrm{pot}}(0),Y_{\mathrm{pot}}(1))=(0,0,0,0)\). Consistency determines the observables. The complete nonzero observed-atom table \(p_n^{(4)}(x,z;d,s,k)\), with \(k=0\) on \(s=0\), is \[\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}x&z&(d,s)&k&p_n^{(4)}\\\hline 0&0&(0,0)&0&.375(1-r_n)\\0&0&(0,1)&0&\lambda_{\mathrm r}/n\\0&0&(0,1)&1&.05(1-r_n)\\0&0&(0,1)&2&.05(1-r_n)-\lambda_{\mathrm r}/n\\0&0&(0,1)&3&.025(1-r_n)\\0&1&(1,0)&0&.25(1-r_n)\\0&1&(1,1)&0&.05(1-r_n)\\0&1&(1,1)&1&.05(1-r_n)\\0&1&(1,1)&2&.05(1-r_n)\\0&1&(1,1)&3&.10(1-r_n)\\1&0&(0,0)&0&.25r_n\\1&0&(0,1)&0&.025r_n\\1&0&(0,1)&1&.075r_n\\1&0&(0,1)&2&.10r_n\\1&0&(0,1)&3&.05r_n\\1&1&(1,0)&0&.25r_n\\1&1&(1,1)&0&.05r_n\\1&1&(1,1)&1&.075r_n\\1&1&(1,1)&2&.075r_n\\1&1&(1,1)&3&.05r_n\end{array}\] and every unlisted atom has mass zero.

definitions.name: Legal realization and relative-transfer handle
definitions.construction: Start from the finite sign, survivor-total, and active-cut decomposition of the unconditional capacity map on the legal tangent-score domains \(\mathcal D_b\); on each piece, lift the required capacity direction to a nearby element of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) by perturbing legal latent response-type masses and instrument propensities. Couple the multinomial score and \(G^*\) through common square-root coordinates, stratify by the common envelope scale, and treat exact zero scale by a separate local-flatness branch. Values of \(d_b\) off \(\mathcal D_b\) are excluded from the lift argument. The target object derived by this handle is the comparison in \(\text{oeq:legal-relative-comparison}\).

statements.statement: The total division operation \(\oslash\) and each coordinate of \(H_x\) are finite semialgebraic functions, while \(F_L\), \(F_U\), and \(m\) are continuous, positively homogeneous, globally Lipschitz, and piecewise linear on a finite polyhedral complex over all of \(\mathbb R^{2K}\). For every \(b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\), \(d_b(g)=\partial_+\bar\Phi(b;g)\) exists and is finite: ordinary quotient rules apply to positive instrument cells, while positive homogeneity together with \(u\oslash0=0\) supplies the ray derivative at empty cells. The map \((b,g)\mapsto d_b(g)\) is jointly semialgebraic and Borel on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\times\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\).
statements.justification: Finite capacity geometry is the reduction that avoids division by vanishing cell-specific survivor masses.
statements.gap: Generic directional-delta results do not supply the zero-cell rational limit or the model-specific finite capacity-face decomposition.
statements.consumer: The legal-face optimizer can enumerate all support and tie configurations needed for reproducible calibration.

statements.statement: If \(b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(p:[0,\eta)\to\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is a one-sided differentiable legal path with \(p(0)=b\), then \(\dot p(0+)\in\mathcal D_b\). For every \(g\in\mathcal D_b\) that is generated by such a legal path, \(d_b(g)\) equals the genuine one-sided derivative \(\partial_+\Phi\{p(t)\}|_{t=0}\). Thus values of \(d_b\) outside \(\mathcal D_b\) provide a total calibration convention but no ambient-to-legal realization theorem.
statements.justification: The domain lemma separates derivatives of legal observed-law paths from algebraic directions introduced solely to make calibration total.
statements.gap: Generic directional calculus does not identify which zero-cell scores arise from the binary-instrument causal-law image.
statements.consumer: The legal realization argument can target exactly the admissible tangent scores without claiming an invalid ambient lift.

statements.statement: The legal observed-law image \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is compact and semialgebraic. For each \(n\), the graph over \(\widehat p\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\) of \(\widehat p\mapsto\{b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}:\|b-\widehat p\|_\infty\le a_n\}\) is compact and semialgebraic; for each fixed \(r>0\), the graph of \(p\mapsto\mathcal B(p,r)\) is compact and semialgebraic. Consequently definable optimization makes \(T_n(g)\) and \(E_{p,r}(g)\) finite Borel value functions of all displayed arguments. With \(G^*=\Sigma(\widehat p_n)^{1/2}W^*\) and the lower-quantile convention, \(c_n\) and the total rectangle \(C_n\) are measurable.
statements.justification: The confidence procedure requires finite optimizers and a measurable conditional critical value on every empirical law.
statements.gap: Directional-bootstrap papers typically impose measurability of the derivative process rather than deriving it from this finite legal semialgebraic image.
statements.consumer: The theorem-level rectangle becomes a genuine statistic suitable for simulation and coverage analysis.

statements.statement: Can the handle in \(\text{def:legal-relative-handle}\) establish, for \(r_n=a_n/2\), \[\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M}P_n\!\left[\sqrt n\|\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(\widehat p_n)-\Phi(p_n)\|_\infty>Q_{1-\alpha}\{E_{p_n,r_n}(G^*)\mid\widehat p_n\},\ B_n\ne\varnothing,\ M(\widehat p_n)>0\right]\le\alpha,\] together with uniformly vanishing probability of the fallback event \(\{B_n=\varnothing\}\cup\{M(\widehat p_n)=0\}\), including arrays with zero cells, simultaneous active-cut ties, and \(Q_{1-\alpha}\{E_{p_n,r_n}(G^*)\mid\widehat p_n\}\to0\), where each displayed conditional quantile uses the lower-quantile convention?
statements.justification: This is the nonroutine legal-inner-neighborhood and relative-quantile step on which honest support adaptation rests, with the total-procedure fallback accounted for explicitly.
statements.gap: Andrews and Guggenberger obtain uniform inference from standardized moment-statistic representations with positive component variances, and Imai and Okamoto begin from uniformly asymptotically linear endpoint estimators with standard deviations bounded away from zero. Neither result constructs the legal observed-law lift for this changing rational capacity map or transfers its critical value when the full endpoint scale collapses.
statements.consumer: A positive resolution yields honest inference without trimming rare survivor strata; failure on the explicit \(K=4\) array would delimit the feasible adaptation class.

statements.statement: For every deterministic sequence \(a_n\to0\) with \(\sqrt n a_n\to\infty\), the total common-Gaussian rectangle satisfies \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal M}P_n\{\Phi(p_n)\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha.\] The full-plane branch covers identically when \(B_n=\varnothing\) or \(M(\widehat p_n)=0\), and the infimum includes legal arrays with arbitrarily vanishing covariate cells, survivor cells, active-cut gaps, and endpoint variances.
statements.justification: Uniform joint coverage is the headline result and cannot be replaced by endpoint-wise Bonferroni or pointwise bootstrap validity.
statements.gap: Frandsen and Pond start from asymptotically normal bound estimators, whereas the two imported sharp endpoints here undergo changing nonlinear directional limits and may have jointly vanishing scale.
statements.consumer: Clinical and labor applications using survivor-complier ordinal outcomes obtain one honest confidence statement for the entire sharp benefit interval.

statements.statement: If \(p_n=p\) and \(\operatorname{Reg}(p)\), then \[c_n\to_P Q_{1-\alpha}\{\|A_pG_0\|_\infty\},\qquad G_0\sim N\{0,\Sigma(p)\},\] and \(P_n\{\Phi(p)\in C_n\}\to1-\alpha\). Thus \(C_n\) is asymptotically equivalent to the oracle bivariate-Gaussian max-norm rectangle using the common covariance \(A_p\Sigma(p)A_p^{\mathsf T}\).
statements.justification: The theorem certifies that honesty at irregular faces does not impose a first-order calibration penalty at ordinary laws.
statements.gap: Fang and Santos characterize derivative-aware resampling, but do not give exact oracle recovery for this legal rational capacity map with a joint endpoint rectangle.
statements.consumer: Analysts at well-separated laws retain the familiar efficient bivariate-Gaussian critical value rather than a least-favorable Bonferroni constant.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P_n\in\mathcal M\), \(P_n\{B_n=\varnothing\text{ or }M(\widehat p_n)=0\}\to0\) and \(c_n=O_{P_n}(1)\). On the complementary event each coordinate diameter of \(C_n\) is \(2c_n/\sqrt n\); consequently the extended random diameter, including the full-plane fallback on a uniformly negligible event, is \(O_{P_n}(n^{-1/2})\). This holds on arrays with covariate or survivor capacities emerging at order \(n^{-1/2}\) and with lower or upper active-cut gaps tied at order \(n^{-1/2}\).
statements.justification: Rate-adaptive width prevents support robustness from degenerating into a fixed deterministic guard while retaining an honest definition on every sample.
statements.gap: Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen recommend bootstrap care at boundaries but do not establish uniform root-\(n\) joint width through disappearing support and cut ties.
statements.consumer: Studies with rare covariate strata keep confidence widths on the sampling scale with probability tending uniformly to one while maintaining the full target population.

statements.statement: Suppose \(K=4\) and \(m_*\le1/4\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), the response-type masses in \(\text{def:k4-legal-array}\) are nonnegative, sum to one in each covariate cell, satisfy conditional instrument independence, treatment and selected-outcome consistency, global no-defiers, increasing weak selection monotonicity, fair-instrument overlap, and the aggregate mass floor; hence \(Q_n^{(4)}\in\mathcal M\) and the displayed table is exactly \(p_n^{(4)}\). Its unconditional capacities are \(H_0=(1-r_n)(\ell^0,h^0)\) and \(H_1=r_n(\ell^1,h^1)\). The emerging-cell upper cuts are exactly \((.40,.30,.30,.40)\), so two cuts bind simultaneously; its lower and upper benefit masses are \(0\) and \(.30\), while the main-cell masses are \(0\) and \(.20\). The table contains the selected outcome atom \(p_n^{(4)}(0,0;0,1,0)=\lambda_{\mathrm r}/n\), and \[M(p_n^{(4)})=.25+.25r_n,\qquad \Phi(p_n^{(4)})=\left(0,\frac{.8+.4r_n}{1+r_n}\right).\] For either \(a_n=n^{-1/3}\) or \(a_n=n^{-0.49}\), the specific-array legal envelope has \(c_n\to_P\sqrt{1.28}z_{1-\alpha/2}\), the fallback probability tends to zero, \(P_n\{\Phi(p_n^{(4)})\in C_n\}\to1-\alpha\), and \[\sqrt n\{U(\widehat p_n)-U(p_n^{(4)})\}\Rightarrow N(0,1.28).\] The variance follows from the limiting main-cell ratio: its numerator event has probability \(.10\), its denominator event has probability \(.125\), and \(\{.10(.2)^2+.025(.8)^2\}/.125^2=1.28\); the emerging cell contributes deterministic root-\(n\) drift but only \(o_P(1)\) centered root-\(n\) noise.
statements.justification: The proposition is a fully reproducible destructive check in the smallest array containing a rare observed atom, root-\(n\) support emergence, simultaneous cuts, and a degenerate lower endpoint.
statements.gap: No cited paper verifies common-Gaussian legal-face calibration on a survivor-complier array combining an order-\(n^{-1}\) observed atom, order-\(n^{-1/2}\) support emergence, simultaneous ties, and a degenerate endpoint.
statements.consumer: A certified legal-face implementation gains an exact atom-level regression test before attempting the full uniform theorem.

sampling_model.design: For each \(n\), observe an independent sample \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) from the row law \(P_n\in\mathcal M\); rows may vary arbitrarily with \(n\).
sampling_model.units: The number of multinomial atoms \(|\mathcal J|\) is fixed, while their probabilities may vanish with \(n\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument and treatment are binary; the outcome has the fixed ordered support \(\mathcal Y\), and selection is observed.
sampling_model.overlap: The inferential class strengthens the inherited pointwise model only by fixed uniform bounds \(\epsilon\le P_n(Z=1\mid X=x)\le1-\epsilon\) and \(M(p_n)\ge m_*\); individual cells and cut gaps may vanish.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The empirical atom vector \(\widehat p_n\) is the sole first-stage estimator. Algebraic division is totalized by \(u\oslash0=0\), the endpoint center uses \(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(\widehat p_n)=(0,1)\) at zero aggregate empirical mass, and \(C_n=\mathbb R^2\) when that fallback is invoked or the legal base set is empty. The common Gaussian draw is realized through the principal covariance square root, and its measurable critical value uses the lower-quantile convention. No support screening, variance floor, or deterministic calibration guard is used.

estimand_functional: \(\theta_B\in[L(p_Q),U(p_Q)]=\left[\sum_xF_L\{H_x(p_Q)\}/M(p_Q),\sum_xF_U\{H_x(p_Q)\}/M(p_Q)\right]\), by the imported AcceptedSlateBenefit2026 sharp-endpoint theorem

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Sharp bounds and efficient estimation are obtained for a survivor-complier causal effect.
Sharp symbolic bounds are derived for ordinal probability-of-benefit measures in imperfect trials.
Standard bootstrap consistency is equivalent to full differentiability under a Gaussian first stage.
The numerical directional delta method is uniformly valid for convex Lipschitz transformations under stated conditions.
A common Gaussian critical value yields simultaneous rectangles for asymptotically normal bound estimators.

Theorems 1--2 establish uniformly valid multiplier-bootstrap confidence bands for infinite-dimensional interval-valued parameters under uniformly asymptotically linear endpoint representations and nondegenerate Gaussian-process variances.

Theorems 1--2 establish uniform asymptotic validity of subsampling and plug-in asymptotic confidence sets for standardized moment-inequality statistics under their stated representation and positive-variance conditions.
Several high-level partial-identification assumptions are constraint qualifications with stringent geometry.
The LP value is not uniformly consistently estimable without restricting the distribution class.
Iterative randomized Lindeberg interpolation improves Gaussian and bootstrap approximation errors for maxima.
Weak coordinate-variance decay yields near-parametric bootstrap rates for high-dimensional maxima.
Gaussian maxima admit scale-free density and anti-concentration bounds for arbitrary covariance matrices.
Discrete causal bounds are represented by optimization over admissible response-function distributions.

tldr: The accepted \(\text{pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport}\) theorem supplies the sharp probability-of-benefit interval among survivor compliers as a ratio of finite capacity extrema; identification is therefore substrate, not a new result. The inferential proposal totalizes every capacity ratio and directional derivative, derives finite Borel legal-base envelopes, and calibrates both endpoint errors with one measurable conditional Gaussian max norm, using a full-plane fallback whenever the legal base set is empty or aggregate empirical mass is zero. Its theorem-level target is uniform joint coverage without lower bounds on individual survivor cells, cut gaps, or endpoint variances; exact bivariate-Gaussian calibration is recovered on separated regular faces, and width is \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) on root-\(n\) support-emergence and tied-cut arrays. The unresolved mathematical core is a legal observed-law inner-neighborhood comparison combined with relative critical-value transfer when the entire envelope scale vanishes.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent settles sharp identification for the finite ordered survivor-complier benefit interval. Existing inference results either impose fixed-law differentiability, start from supplied asymptotically linear endpoint or standardized moment representations, or require geometric and positive-variance regularity that excludes changing support and a jointly collapsing endpoint scale.
project_justification.niche: The finite binary-instrument model permits exact capacity geometry and multinomial coupling, yet legality of nearby observed laws is more restrictive than ambient perturbation of a probability vector. This creates a tractable model-specific route to uniform inference at zero cells and tied extrema.
project_justification.fill: The total legal-base envelope retains every nearby support and cut face, uses one Gaussian draw for both endpoints, and seeks a scale-homogeneous comparison yielding honest coverage over all legal triangular arrays while reverting to the exact oracle rectangle on separated faces.

related_work: The accepted CausalSmith result pid\_slate\_benefit\_partialtransport, Theorem thm:sharp-exact-mass-threshold-interval, is imported verbatim as the identification substrate: it proves the exact endpoint formula and full-law sharpness under the inherited finite covariate, finite ordered outcome, binary-instrument selection model. Angrist, Imbens, and Rubin (1996) support conditional instrument randomization, treatment consistency, and global no-defiers; Dong and Heiler (2026), Assumptions 3.1--3.2, support treatment-mediated selection and outcome consistency together with covariate-specific weak selection monotonicity. The fixed \(\epsilon\) overlap bound and fixed \(m_*\) aggregate denominator floor are strengthened uniform-class restrictions here, not claims attributed to Kennedy, Harris, and Keele (2019). Kennedy, Harris, and Keele define survivor-complier mean effects and provide fixed-law efficient inference, so their work informs the population and inferential comparison only. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) derive sharp symbolic ordinal benefit bounds and identify confidence intervals at boundaries as an open inferential issue. Fang and Santos (2019) show why ordinary bootstrap inference fails for nonlinear directional derivatives and motivate resampling the derivative itself. Hong and Li (2018) approximate directional derivatives numerically, with uniform validity for convex Lipschitz maps under additional Gaussian-boundary conditions. Frandsen and Pond (2025) calibrate common rectangles when endpoint estimators already possess a joint asymptotically normal representation. Imai and Okamoto (2026), Theorems 1--2 and Assumptions 1 and 5, establish uniformly valid multiplier-bootstrap bands for infinite-dimensional interval-valued parameters from supplied uniformly asymptotically linear endpoint estimators and Gaussian-process variances bounded away from zero; those conditions do not construct the legal observed-law derivative of this changing rational capacity map and rule out a jointly collapsing endpoint scale. Andrews and Guggenberger (2009), Theorems 1--2 and equation (3.3), prove uniform validity for subsampling and plug-in procedures built from standardized moment-inequality statistics with positive component variances; that representation neither realizes capacity directions inside the legal causal-law image nor supplies relative calibration when all endpoint variation vanishes. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2022) demonstrate that the geometric qualifications behind partial-identification inference are substantive and model-specific. Voronin (2025) gives pointwise LP-value inference and proves that unrestricted uniform consistency is impossible, motivating exploitation of the survivor model's special legal geometry. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike (2022), Lopes, Lin, and Müller (2020), and Vijaykumar (2026) inform the Gaussian-max comparison, but do not provide relative critical-value transfer when the entire scale collapses. Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser (2024) center legal discrete causal laws in sharp-bound computation; the present target is the distinct local legal perturbation theorem required for inference.
technical_internal_limitation: The finite unconditional-capacity reduction, legal tangent-domain result, definable measurability result, regular-face oracle calculation, tight critical-value argument, and explicit \(K=4\) legal array do not prove \(\text{oeq:legal-relative-comparison}\). Algebraic values \(d_b(g)\) for \(g\notin\mathcal D_b\) make optimization total but provide no ambient-to-legal lift. Even on \(\mathcal D_b\), the capacity direction required for domination must still be realized by nearby legal observed laws, and additive weak-convergence error is insufficient when the common critical radius vanishes. The total procedure is defined on every sample: \(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}=(0,1)\) at zero empirical aggregate mass and \(C_n=\mathbb R^2\) there or when \(B_n\) is empty. A reproducible coverage deficit or persistent legal-versus-ambient mismatch beyond the certified \(\text{prop:k4-kill-test}\) array stops the proposed construction.
honest_scope: Sharp identification is imported from AcceptedSlateBenefit2026 and is not a contribution of this proposal. Treatment-indexed selection and outcomes are inherited structural definitions; conditional IV randomization, treatment consistency, and no-defiers follow the Angrist--Imbens--Rubin IV model, while weak selection monotonicity follows Dong--Heiler. Fixed \(\epsilon\) overlap and fixed \(m_*\) aggregate survivor mass are strengthened uniform-class conditions. Total algebraic division, the off-domain derivative convention, and the full-plane branch make the statistic finite and measurable; off-domain values do not assert a legal tangent lift. The regular-face theorem, root-\(n\) width, and explicit atom-level \(K=4\) diagnostic have direct proof traction. Uniform joint coverage remains conditional on resolving the legal inner-neighborhood and collapsing-scale relative-transfer question. No lower bound on an individual cell probability, cut gap, or endpoint variance is introduced. Under a fixed separated law, the proposal reduces to the standard bivariate multinomial delta method and its exact Gaussian max-norm critical value.
